segments.text: Next, Nacayam, Sushakti, Nirmitu, Bhut, Bahu, Shri, Revato, Asya, Janma, Devanda, Kachetam.
This yogi has created his gross, elementary body and subtle body of emotions by his own
Sathandrushakti.
Sushakti, Nirmitu, Bhut, Bahu, Shri, Revata.
He has created, Nirmita, he has created Sushakti by his own Sathandriya, by his own independent
way of Chaitanya.
What has he created?
Bhut, Bahu, Shri, Revata.
Bhut, Shri, Revata, Bhut, Shri, Revata, Bhut, Shri, Revata.
Bhut, Shri, Revata means elementary body, Bahu, Shri, Revata means subtle body, subtle
body that plays in dreaming and dreamless state.
And elementary body, that functions in waking, waking place, waking, wakefulness.
This is Bhut, Shri, Revata and that is Bahu, Shri, Revata.
For him, there is no bondage of birth and death, no asya, Janma, Devanda, Kachetam.
This is what he says in the next sutra, Vidya, Avinashya, Janma, Avinashya.
As his knowledge is established in continuity, Vidya, Avinashya, Vidya, his knowledge of
self, his knowledge of being, Avinashya, he is established in continuity, Avinashya.
When his knowledge is permanent, then Janma, Avinashya, question of repeated birth and
death does not arise for him.
Janma, by Janma, you must understand that Janma and Marna, both, life and death does not arise
for him.
He never gets birth nor dies.
Proktaya, Sahaja Vidya, Avinashya, when this pure knowledge of consciousness, Shuddha
Vidya, is Avinashya, in continuity, established in continuity.
What is that?
Satyata unma-ganata-ya-sufra-ne, when that pure knowledge is established in continuity,
then Janma-na, Janma is gone forever.
For him, there is no more Janma, there is no more birth.
It means that there is no more death also.
Aganasa-hakaari-karma-hya-tukasya-dukhama-ya-ya-sya, de-hindra-ya-jya-sama-ya-ya-ya-sya-na-shya-ya.
What is Janma?
Janma is caused by action, action, that action which is attached with ignorance, that action
which is attached, where ignorance is being attached to that karma.
By that action, body, organs, and all those limbs, et cetera, of body are created.
Action is the creator of these things, body and organs.
So when action which is attached by ignorance, when that action is over, when the cause is
over, the effect does not remain, the effect is also over, effect means Janma, effect means
being created, being born, that with Damsa-sampaneva, that noise is already there.
So there is no no more death for him and no more birth for him.
Tukasya-trikantya, in Trikantya-sastra, it is said,
Sapa-pancham parit-te-je-he-ho-pade-e-leksanam, trinadi-kam, tatha-parnam, pashanam, satcharachanam,
Shiva-devanya-parivantam, bhava-bhubram-hitam, Sarvam-siv-mayam, dya-ta-bhu-yo-janma-na-pava-pravna-ya.
The one who has abandoned parit-te-je, along with its offshoots and along with this is right
and this is wrong, along with the perception, perceiving right and wrong, who has left it
aside, who has kept these things aside, then for him blades of grass, parnam, leaves, pashanam,
rocks, innate and not innate, Shiva-devanya-parivantam, right from Shiva to prithvi, right from Shiva to
Avani means prithvi, bhava-bhubram-hitam, existent objects or non-existent objects, existent objects
are what we feel already, non-existent objects are what we imagine, Sarvam-siv-mayam-dya-ta-devanya
who realizes all this as one with Lord Shiva-bhu-yo-janma-na-pava-pravna-ya.
He never comes again in this world, he is never born, he is satchande.
And Sarvam-siv-dya-ta-devanya-parivantam is also said, Saniv-vanam-param-shuddham-guru-param-paragatam,
tath Vidyat-to-aviyam-cce-ta-gatt-to-aviyo-nujane, jaye de.
Saniv-vanam-when one is free, where one is liberated from repeated birth and death, when one is established
in one's own consciousness. That's supreme, pure, shudham, pure, Guru-pāram-pāram-pāram-pāram.
Which is being realized by the success you, teachings of masters. Guru-pāram-pāram-pāram-pāram.
Success you teachings from one to another, from one to another, huh?
When the one who realizes that, he becomes mukta, būyo nājaide. He never comes in this universe again.
Mṛti jīti apī. In Nētra Tandrār, so it is said.
You by adopting the divine yoga path.
By adopting the divine yoga path, that supreme, eternal, stable, and beyond three-fold states of being.
When that being is experienced, then he does not come again in this world. Rīstva, būyo nājaide.
